overview: A long, left-trending granite ridge line up the lower-right side of Dragontail's north face, mixing clean crack-and-corner pitches with looser scrambling, capped by the striking 'Fin' feature near the summit.

face: North Face, entry couloir

face: North Face (lowest point, between Triple Couloirs and Backbone Ridge)

face: West/Southwest side, via Colchuck Glacier and Colchuck Col

face: North Face (center, three couloirs)
overview: An ultra-classic Cascades alpine line: three couloirs separated by short steep rock bands cut straight up the middle of Dragontail's north face, giving roughly 2,500 ft of sustained snow, ice, and mixed climbing to the summit.

face: North face, right (NW) side — above the Colchuck Glacier
overview: A long, high-quality granite line up the right (west) side of Dragontail's north face, roughly 200 ft right of Backbone Ridge, following corners and crack systems to two sustained 5.8 crux pitches before ridge scrambling to the summit.

face: West side of the peak

face: Southwest ridge / summit block

face: Northeast side, wrapping to the north side (talus approach and scramble line)

face: Southwest ridge / south side of the peak

face: East side (Standup Creek drainage)
overview: A quieter, less-traveled alternate approach to Earl Peak's summit from the east via the Standup Creek Trail, which gains a ridge/saddle joining the same upper scramble used by the Southwest Ridge route.

route: Northeast Buttress ("Come Over to the Dark Side")
face: Northeast buttress / upper north face
overview: A long, sustained new-wave buttress route up East McMillan Spire's dramatic 2,400-foot northeast wall, climbing compact Skagit gneiss on mostly moderate (5.6-5.8) rock with a handful of 5.9 pitches and three or four pitches of 5.10-.

face: West side, approached via the col shared with West McMillan Spire
overview: East McMillan Spire (7,992 ft) is the lower, eastern summit of the McMillan Spires, twin granite towers just 0.14 mile apart in the Southern Pickets, North Cascades National Park. It sits directly across a low-fifth-class connecting ridge from its taller twin,

face: North Buttress
overview: A nine-pitch, 2,000-foot buttress route up East Twin Needle's north side, first climbed in 2022 along a line envisioned decades earlier by North Cascades historian John Roper.

face: South gullies to the Eye Col, then the summit block above it
overview: East Twin Needle (7,868 ft) is the eastern and slightly lower of the Twin Needles pinnacles in the Southern Pickets, 0.55 mi west of Mount Terror and just east of its taller sister summit, West Twin Needle (7,936 ft). William Degenhardt, James Martin, and Herb

face: North side, central couloir
overview: A 1,200-foot mixed snow/ice/rock couloir splitting the north side of the Twin Needles, first climbed in June 2009.

face: South Buttress of The Blob (aka The Rake)
overview: A long, moderate alpine rock line up the right-edge buttress of "The Blob," the rock formation just north of the Himmelhorn in the Southern Pickets, finishing across the exposed "Bela Lugosi Traverse" and up a summit dihedral.

face: South side, gained via the Stetattle Ridge/Stetattle Creek approach

face: Southeast basin/notch route, between Emerald and Cardinal Peak

face: West side gully/erosion feature to the twin summit block
overview: A distinct, dedicated line on the peak: an easy class 3 scramble to Emerald's twin summit block via an erosion-carved gully on the peak's west side, reached from the same North Fork Entiat trailhead (or alternately from Lake Chelan via the Emerald Park Trail).

rock_grade: Class 2-3, finishing with roughly 15 ft of exposed 3rd-class scrambling onto the true summit block
face: East ridge/shoulder between Prusik Pass and the true (NE) summit — the opposite side of the peak from the SW/Aasgard-side scramble
overview: The most-traveled, standard line up Enchantment Peak: reach Prusik Pass from the core Enchantment basin, then work west along the peak's east ridge over a couple of minor humps to a short, exposed 3rd-class step onto the small, flat true summit block.

rock_grade: Class 2-3, with a short, loose 3rd-class gully below the summit plateau (an exposed 4th-class (some say low 5th) option exists onto the more exposed SW sub-summit but is not required for the true high point)
face: South-side gully below the northeast (true) summit, reached across the core basin from the Aasgard Pass side — the opposite side of the peak from the Prusik Pass east ridge
overview: Enchantment Peak (8,538 ft) is the granite high point of the Core Enchantments, rising on the ridge between Prusik Peak (NE) and Dragontail Peak/Aasgard Pass (SW), within the Alpine Lakes Wilderness. The peak actually has two summits about 1,500 ft apart and o

face: East side of the East Peak, above the North Fork Teanaway River
overview: An obscure, unpolished Class 3-4 (low 5th) gully line up the east side of Esmeralda's East Peak — by no means a classic, with the crux low in the gully on wet, friable rock.
